change.title: Serialize canonical config writers across processes
change.summary: Adds one persistent credential-free writer fence inside the pinned config directory, acquires it after the process-local config gate and before every canonical config load-modify-save, migration, downgrade, backup, or full save publication, and verifies with competing real child processes that stale snapshots cannot overwrite an earlier writer.

basis: the process-local config access gate is always acquired before the cross-process writer fence, preserving one lock order
canonical config update, fallible update, full save, migration-capable load, downgrade, and rolling-backup publication use the same persistent writer lock inode
the lock file is credential-free, no-follow, single-link, mode 0600, opened relative to the pinned config directory, and identity-rechecked after blocking acquisition
read-only canonical consumer projection does not create or acquire the writer fence and atomic config rename/read behavior remains unchanged

two real child test processes require the second writer to observe kernel EWOULDBLOCK before release, prove it cannot enter read-modify-write while the first holds the fence, and then preserve both committed fields
negative tests reject a symlink, a hard-linked lock inode, and a directory-entry replacement while a second writer waits, without publishing the rejected config mutation
schema, DTOs, visible text, one-click/history behavior, atomic rollback behavior, and runtime receipt semantics remain unchanged
focused Rust tests, quality metadata validation, documentation governance, exact-SHA source gate, and clean-context review are required for source closure

typed commit outcomes, expected-record CAS for every full-snapshot restore, multi-file history/authority transactions, coordinator decomposition, artifact, installed, live provider or Science, signing, and release behavior remain excluded
